title: Space & Astronomy
description: 36 original questions on planets, moons, constellations, telescopes, and space missions with local SVG diagrams.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which planet in our Solar System is illustrated with its iconic icy ring system?
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings span up to 282,000 km across yet are often only tens of meters thick.

questions.prompt: What celestial event occurs when the Moon passes directly between the Sun and Earth, as illustrated here?
questions.explanation: During a total solar eclipse, the Moon blocks the Sun's bright disk, revealing the solar corona.

questions.prompt: Which famous constellation features the iconic three-star belt illustrated here?
questions.explanation: Orion's Belt consists of Alnitak, Alnilam, and Mintaka, flanked by Betelgeuse and Rigel.

questions.prompt: Which infrared space telescope uses the 18 hexagonal gold-coated mirror segments illustrated here?
questions.explanation: Launched in December 2021, JWST orbits the Sun-Earth L2 point 1.5 million km away.

questions.prompt: Which lunar phase is shown when less than half of the Moon's illuminated disk is visible as a curved sliver?
questions.explanation: A waxing or waning crescent appears before or after the New Moon.

questions.prompt: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits the Sun at an average distance of about 58 million km.

questions.prompt: Which planet is the hottest in our Solar System due to its runaway greenhouse atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, raising surface temperatures above 460°C.

questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the 'Red Planet' because of iron oxide dust on its surface?
questions.explanation: Rusty iron oxide minerals give Mars its signature reddish hue.

questions.prompt: What is the largest planet in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other Solar System planets combined.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our Solar System?
questions.explanation: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy containing 100 to 400 billion stars.

questions.prompt: Who was the first human to walk on the Moon in July 1969?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface during NASA's Apollo 11 mission.

questions.prompt: Who was the first human to travel into outer space (1961)?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin completed one orbit of Earth aboard Vostok 1 on April 12, 1961.

questions.prompt: What is the closest star to Earth after the Sun?
questions.explanation: Proxima Centauri is a red dwarf star about 4.24 light-years away.

questions.prompt: What is the brightest star in Earth's night sky?
questions.explanation: Sirius in Canis Major is roughly 8.6 light-years from Earth.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest moon in our Solar System, orbiting Jupiter?
questions.explanation: Ganymede is larger than the planet Mercury and has its own magnetic field.

questions.prompt: Which moon of Saturn is the only moon in the Solar System with a dense atmosphere and liquid surface lakes?
questions.explanation: Titan's lakes and rivers are made of liquid methane and ethane.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest known volcano and mountain in the Solar System, located on Mars?
questions.explanation: Olympus Mons rises nearly 22 km above the Martian plains — nearly three times Mount Everest's height.

questions.prompt: Which planet rotates on its side with an axial tilt of about 98 degrees?
questions.explanation: Uranus essentially rolls around the Sun on its side, causing extreme 42-year-long polar seasons.

questions.prompt: Which planet in our Solar System rotates backward (retrograde) relative to most other planets?
questions.explanation: On Venus, the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the massive, centuries-old anticyclonic storm on Jupiter?
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is larger than the entire planet Earth.

questions.prompt: Approximately how long does sunlight take to travel from the Sun to Earth?
questions.explanation: Light travels at ~300,000 km/s across the 150 million km Earth–Sun distance in 8 min 20 sec.

questions.prompt: Which spacecraft, launched in 1977, became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space?
questions.explanation: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in August 2012.

questions.prompt: Which famous comet returns to the inner Solar System roughly every 75 to 76 years?
questions.explanation: Halley's Comet last appeared in 1986 and is due back in 2061.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the major spiral galaxy closest to the Milky Way?
questions.explanation: Andromeda lies about 2.5 million light-years away and will merge with the Milky Way in ~4.5 billion years.

questions.prompt: Which moon of Jupiter is considered a prime candidate for extraterrestrial life due to its subsurface saltwater ocean?
questions.explanation: Europa's icy crust hides a global ocean warmed by tidal flexing from Jupiter.

questions.prompt: Which is the most volcanically active body in the Solar System, orbiting Jupiter?
questions.explanation: Io has over 400 active volcanoes powered by intense tidal heating.

questions.prompt: In 2006, the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as what type of object?
questions.explanation: Pluto shares its orbital neighborhood in the Kuiper Belt with other icy bodies.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape?
questions.explanation: The event horizon marks the point of no return around a black hole.

questions.prompt: Which giant canyon system on Mars stretches over 4,000 km, dwarfing Earth's Grand Canyon?
questions.explanation: Valles Marineris is up to 7 km deep and 200 km wide.

questions.prompt: Which NASA rover landed in Jezero Crater on Mars in 2021 carrying the Ingenuity helicopter?
questions.explanation: Ingenuity achieved the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the supermassive black hole at the center of our Milky Way galaxy?
questions.explanation: Sagittarius A* has a mass roughly 4 million times that of our Sun.

questions.prompt: What is the distance light travels in one Julian year (~9.46 trillion km) called?
questions.explanation: A light-year is a unit of distance, not time.

questions.prompt: What is the region of icy bodies beyond Neptune's orbit that includes Pluto called?
questions.explanation: The Kuiper Belt extends roughly from 30 to 50 astronomical units from the Sun.

questions.prompt: What are the two small, irregularly shaped moons of Mars named?
questions.explanation: Their names mean 'fear' and 'dread' in Greek mythology.

questions.prompt: Which space probe flew past Pluto in 2015, revealing its famous heart-shaped nitrogen glacier?
questions.explanation: Tombaugh Regio is the bright heart-shaped plain on Pluto.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the phenomenon where a massive star ends its life in a colossal luminous explosion?
questions.explanation: Supernovae forge and disperse heavy elements like gold and iron into space.
